headline: Sellers Take the Wheel on Wednesday as Energy and Software Bear the Brunt
body_html:
Wednesday's session ended on a cautious note, with declining issues outnumbering advancers 309 to 234 across a universe of 545 names. The Federal Reserve's first interest-rate increase in three years dominated the macro conversation, rattling rate-sensitive pockets of the market and reinforcing a defensive tilt that had been building through much of the morning. Energy was the day's clearest casualty, shedding more than three percent as a sector, while Homebuilders and Software each surrendered roughly one percent.

Against that defensive backdrop, Healthcare and Consumer names eked out slim gains — up 0.21 and 0.20 percent, respectively — suggesting investors were rotating toward perceived stability rather than growth. Materials and Industrials also managed to stay in the black, albeit modestly, as pockets of industrial demand held firm despite the broader risk-off mood.

The session's standout mover was Forgent Power Solutions, which surged 11.1 percent to lead all gainers, closely trailed by Semtech's 11.03-percent advance. On the other end, JB Hunt absorbed the sharpest single-stock blow of the day, tumbling 13.3 percent in what was a bruising session for the intermodal freight operator. With the Fed's new hiking cycle now officially underway, Thursday's price action will be the first real test of how the market digests tighter policy beyond the initial shock.

briefs.headline: Fed Pulls the Trigger on Its First Rate Hike in Three Years
briefs.body: The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate Wednesday for the first time since 2023, marking a pivotal shift in monetary policy. The move rattled growth-sensitive sectors while lifting the case for defensive positioning. Traders are now closely parsing guidance for the pace of any additional increases ahead.

briefs.headline: JB Hunt Leads All Decliners With a 13-Percent Shellacking
briefs.body: Shares of JB Hunt fell 13.3 percent Wednesday, the steepest single-session loss in the universe, as the intermodal freight carrier faced pressure on multiple fronts. The drop underscored lingering anxiety over transportation demand at a moment when tighter financial conditions could further squeeze shipping volumes.

briefs.headline: Energy Names Battered as Sector Drops More Than Three Percent
briefs.body: Energy was Wednesday's worst-performing sector, sliding 3.17 percent on the session. Magnolia Oil & Gas fell 8.58 percent, Range Resources dropped 7.28 percent, and Core Laboratories gave back 6.61 percent, reflecting a broad exodus from commodity-linked names as the rate-hike backdrop darkened the demand outlook.

briefs.headline: Boeing Chief Concedes 737 Max Ramp-Up Is Running Behind Schedule
briefs.body: Boeing's chief executive acknowledged Wednesday that stabilizing 737 Max production is taking longer than the company had originally anticipated. The admission adds to a string of operational setbacks for the manufacturer and may weigh on delivery timelines for airline customers already navigating a competitive capacity environment.

briefs.headline: Premium Cabin Demand Reshapes American Airlines Revenue Mix
briefs.body: American Airlines disclosed that roughly 30 percent of its seat inventory is now responsible for half of total revenue, a figure that underscores the accelerating shift toward premium-cabin travel. The airline's commentary adds to a growing body of evidence that carriers leaning into higher-margin cabin classes are finding a durable source of pricing power.

briefs.headline: Costco Broadens Rapid-Delivery Reach Across Nearly All U.S. States
briefs.body: Costco extended its delivery arrangement with Uber Eats to cover 47 states, significantly widening the warehouse retailer's same-day fulfillment footprint. The expansion positions Costco to capture a broader slice of on-demand grocery spending and deepens a partnership that has been gaining traction since its initial rollout.
